SYSTEM SOFTWARE
DENNIS RITCHIE
BELL LABS
POINTERS AND STRUCTURES
C is a general-purpose, procedural programming language
C is developed in the early 1970s.
C is developed by Dennis Ritchie.
C is developed at Bell Labs.
C was designed primarily for system programming.
C was designed specifically for writing operating systems.
Creation of C was closely tied to the development of the Unix operating system.
C is known for its simplicity, efficiency, and close-to-hardware capabilities.
C allows programmers to manage memory and control hardware directly.
C operates at a low level but is still high level enough to write structured and modular programs.
Syntax of C has influenced many later languages.
C influenced the syntax of C++, Java, and Python.
One of the defining characteristics of C is its portability.
C's portability means its programs run on different hardware with little or no modification.
C's portability made it a popular choice for system and application software.
C provides a rich set of operators
C provides a rich set of data types
Arrays, pointers, and structures are few data types used in C.
C provides a rich set of control flow statements
C allows programmers to closely manage a computer’s memory and processor.
Despite being a relatively old language, C remains widely used.
C is widely used for embedded systems, OS development, and high-performance applications.
